U nited K ingdom. — The following is a summary o f the results 
of a retrospective study of the incidence o f mumps covering the 
period 1961-1967, and a prospective study from A p ril 1969 to 
December 1971.
In the retrospective study, based on inform ation supplied by 
a number o f collaborating general practitioners, all cases of mumps 
reported between the beginning o f 1961 and the end o f 1967 were 
recorded by age and sex and by the presence or absence of complications. The overall rate was 6.6 cases of mumps per 1 000 patients 
per year. 
The peak age incidence was among 5-14 year olds

summary.text: Summarises, in English and French, two United Kingdom general-practice studies of mumps: a retrospective review of 1961–1967 and a prospective study from 1969 to 1971. It reports an overall rate of 6.6 cases per 1,000 patients a year, peak incidence in 5–14-year-olds and equal sex distribution, with orchitis and encephalitis as the main complications. Complications were more frequent in people over 15 and in high-incidence years, and most encephalitis patients had no lasting effects.
